title: Add structured output example (JSON Schema) with validation + retry-on-parse-failure guidance
author: Sabrina James
description: Adds a canonical Python example for structured outputs using JSON Schema, including (1) strict schema definition, (2) response validation, and (3) a retry strategy for the two failure modes we see most often in support: invalid JSON / parse failures and schema mismatch. This aligns the Python SDK example with the event/terminology decisions in ENG-2842 and the docs refresh work, and addresses SUP-18433 where a customer copied an older snippet and hit a schema mismatch error. The example is intentionally copy/paste runnable, avoids unsafe patterns (no eval/exec, no trusting unvalidated JSON), and demonstrates a minimal but production-appropriate retry loop with bounded attempts + backoff. It also documents when NOT to retry (auth/4xx, timeouts) and how to surface structured validation errors to callers. The unit tests cover: successful structured decode, malformed JSON from the model, missing required fields, extra properties when additionalProperties=false, and ensuring we do not accidentally “repair” JSON in a way that hides a real schema problem. Follow-ups: once docs PR lands, we should link docs -> this file and deprecate the older JSON-mode snippet in the README (tracked separately).

conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): Can we ensure the retry loop only triggers on parse/validation errors and not on any API errors? Also would like the terminology to match the docs refresh: “structured output” (not “JSON mode”).

Sabrina James (author): Updated: retry now only catches (a) JSONDecodeError and (b) jsonschema.ValidationError. API exceptions re-raise. Also replaced “JSON mode” wording with “structured output” everywhere in the example and README.

Brian Murphy (review): Schema looks good. One nit: please set additionalProperties=false to match our guidelines and include an example of required fields. Also add a note about schema versioning (we’ve seen older snippets drifting).

Sabrina James (author): Done. Schema now sets additionalProperties=false and required=[...]. Added a short comment about versioning strategy and keeping schema changes backwards-compatible (or bump schema version) per standards.

Marcus Lin (security review): Please avoid printing raw model output on parse failure (it can contain user data). If we log anything, it should be truncated/redacted. Also make sure we don’t encourage “JSON repair” via regex in docs.

Sabrina James (author): Good catch. Removed printing the raw completion; now we log a short, truncated message with attempt count only. Also added an explicit “Don’t: regex-repair JSON” note in the guidance section.
Elliot Price (docs): Can we add a short section describing strict vs lenient parsing and why we recommend strict by default? This will be mirrored into the docs-site page.
Sabrina James (author): Added a short section at the bottom of the example describing strict vs lenient parsing. Default path stays strict; lenient is framed as a last resort with clear trade-offs.
Ibrahim Khan (review): Looks aligned with ENG-2842 now. Please add a unit test proving we don’t retry forever and that backoff is bounded.
Sabrina James (author): Added test_structured_output_retry_bounds to assert max_attempts honored and backoff computation is capped. Pushed update.
release_notes: Python SDK: added canonical structured output example using JSON Schema with validation and bounded retries on parse/validation failures.
Clarified guidance: do not log raw model outputs on failures; avoid unsafe JSON “repair” patterns.
Added tests covering common failure modes (malformed JSON, missing required fields, additionalProperties violations).
